decision: oceancube owns field-to-field transformation, physical and geometric fields, I/O, metadata, storage, and visualization; it does not own ecological indicators
rationale: Preserves a coherent upstream data-cube and physical-field role
revisit_trigger: A proposed feature cannot be classified as field preparation, physical diagnosis, geometry, storage, or visualization

decision: spatind owns indicator construction, indicator time series, uncertainty, trend inference, breakpoints, and regime interpretation
rationale: Separates downstream ecological/statistical meaning from upstream field transformations
revisit_trigger: A versioned downstream contract demonstrates a necessary shared responsibility

decision: cube_trend remains a descriptive per-cell elapsed-time ordinary linear slope
rationale: The current tested contract is descriptive field transformation and contains no inference
source: current source, tests, man page, handbook, and maintainer roadmap contract
revisit_trigger: A separately approved breaking-contract proposal

decision: Sen slopes, Mann-Kendall tests, p-values, breakpoints, and regime shifts are excluded from oceancube
rationale: These methods express inference over derived series rather than cube representation
revisit_trigger: A shared generic field-inference contract is proposed with compelling evidence

decision: oceancube will not reimplement TEOS-10 equations and will delegate thermodynamic calculations to gsw
rationale: TEOS-10 has an authoritative maintained implementation and numerical validation suite
source: TEOS-10 and GSW-R official documentation; maintainer roadmap contract
revisit_trigger: gsw becomes unavailable or ceases to implement the authoritative standard

decision: oceancube prepares renderer-neutral scientific 3-D data and keeps the renderer replaceable
rationale: Scientific preparation, decimation, orientation, and provenance must not depend on one graphics package
source: user-driven requirement; ggcube, OceanView, and rgl review; maintainer roadmap contract
revisit_trigger: A stable renderer-neutral contract proves impossible after prototypes

decision: hardening measurement infrastructure precedes CF, vertical, vector, and 3-D feature expansion
rationale: Architectural complexity needs real-data, parity, coverage, benchmark, and stress baselines
revisit_trigger: All Gate A baselines exist and the hardening exit review is approved

decision: vertical coordinate semantics and primitives precede named vertical diagnostics
rationale: Named diagnostics cannot be reliable without orientation, units, interpolation, masking, and edge rules
source: oce and TEOS-10 review; maintainer roadmap contract
revisit_trigger: Vertical contract and primitive design are approved

decision: grid topology, metrics, and component positions precede vector alignment and vector calculus
rationale: Staggered and curvilinear model fields require explicit positions and metric-aware operations
source: xgcm official documentation; maintainer roadmap contract
revisit_trigger: Grid contract and metric test suite are approved

decision: the oceancube-to-spatind exchange will be a versioned plain-data contract with stable keys and explicit units
rationale: The packages need an auditable boundary without sharing live backends or hidden state
revisit_trigger: A downstream prototype identifies missing keys or semantics

decision: small and medium 3-D surfaces and slices are separated from large volumetric rendering and long animations
rationale: The latter require decimation, memory estimation, lazy execution, and chunk planning
source: ggcube and rgl review; maintainer roadmap contract
revisit_trigger: Performance evidence supports moving a workload between scale classes

decision: xarray, Dask, kerchunk, and xgcm are architectural references and do not create a Python core dependency
rationale: oceancube remains an R package while adopting proven separation and scheduling concepts selectively
source: official project documentation; maintainer roadmap contract
revisit_trigger: A separately approved optional adapter has a bounded dependency and maintenance plan

decision: stars, terra, sf, ncdfCF, OceanView, ggcube, and rgl are optional adapters, reference implementations, or inspiration rather than substitutes for ocean_cube
rationale: The canonical cube contract must remain stable across external tool lifecycles
source: official R ecosystem documentation; maintainer roadmap contract
revisit_trigger: Adapter prototypes show a narrower or stronger dependency strategy

decision: future public API growth must favor small composable engines, arguments, methods, and adapters rather than one export per historical idea
rationale: The 0.2.0 audit found approximately 114 proposals and demonstrated the maintenance risk of API inflation
revisit_trigger: A proposed export passes an explicit API necessity review

decision: choose a native, ncdfCF-backed, or hybrid CF interpretation engine
rationale: CF coverage, control, dependency weight, and conformance need prototype evidence
revisit_trigger: CF prototype and conformance-oracle comparison are complete

decision: choose one-way or round-trip conversion semantics for stars and terra adapters
rationale: Lossless dimensions, metadata, lazy state, and write-back guarantees differ by target
revisit_trigger: Adapter feasibility matrix and round-trip tests exist

decision: select optional 3-D renderer or renderer set
rationale: ggcube and rgl have different static, interactive, WebGL, animation, and deployment tradeoffs
revisit_trigger: Renderer-neutral surface prototype and platform matrix exist

decision: select the public lazy-NetCDF entry contract without assuming a new function
rationale: read_nc materializes while the bounded deferred backend is internal; compatibility options need review
revisit_trigger: API option paper covers ocean_cube descriptor input, read_nc mode, and a possible opener

decision: place the minimal versioned provenance contract in 0.3.0-A as P0 and extend scientific metadata integration in 0.3.0-B
rationale: A4a selects the flat-primary plus flat-secondary hybrid; A4b1 proves the core engine; A4b2 proves the linear core rollout; A4b3a proves temporal, multi-input and wrapper rollout; A4b3b migrates all identified remaining runtime producers; global A4-EXIT certification is pending
source: post-release audit; maintainer roadmap contract; A4a design contracts; A4b1 executable core; A4b2 linear runtime evidence; A4b3a temporal and multi-input evidence; A4b3b table, geometry and remaining-producer evidence
revisit_trigger: A4-EXIT evidence shows that global V1 compatibility, privacy, serialization, or cross-output lineage cannot be certified

decision: use 0.2.0.9000 for development immediately after stable 0.2.0, with 0.3.0 as the next intended formal release
rationale: The fourth version component distinguishes post-release development without claiming the 0.3.0 release prematurely
revisit_trigger: The project adopts a different development-version convention

decision: keep main as the stable/post-release integration branch and use dev-0.3.0 as the active branch for the 0.3 cycle after deleting the fully merged local dev-0.2.0 branch
rationale: The branch transition occurs only after Gate A approval and preserves the certified main and stable release tag
source: git ancestry audit; maintainer roadmap contract
revisit_trigger: Development complexity requires revisiting the branch policy

decision: choose the optional dependency depth and validation authority for the future spatind exchange
rationale: The downstream API was unavailable when the existing boundary contract was written
revisit_trigger: Accessible spatind repository and prototype consumer exist

decision: choose CFtime, a custom representation, or another strategy for non-Gregorian calendars
rationale: Idealized calendars cannot be represented safely as ordinary Date values
revisit_trigger: Calendar requirements and serialization prototypes are complete

decision: approve licenses, access methods, fixture derivation, redistribution, and offline-CI policy for the exact OISST v2.1, ETOPO 2022 v1 and WOA23 v3.3 governed fixtures
rationale: A3b verifies exact first-party legal evidence, attribution, stable bounded access, deterministic derivation, source/final SHA-256, size policy, byte-identical regeneration and local-only tests; Copernicus and unlisted future sources remain outside this approval
source: provider documentation; dev/hardening/real-data source/legal matrix, fixture policy and A3b executed evidence; committed fixture manifest
revisit_trigger: A new provider/product/version is proposed, exact terms change, a source response drifts, or fixture size/network policy changes

decision: the historical approximately 114-function 0.2.0 proposal is not a future export commitment
rationale: The implemented 0.2.0 contract has 38 exports and later decisions require a smaller composable API
revisit_trigger: Never; retained as historical evidence

decision: the historical Theil-Sen option proposed for cube_slope is superseded by the final cube_trend contract
rationale: Current tested behavior is elapsed-time ordinary linear slope and inference belongs downstream
source: historical 0.2.0 scope; current cube_trend source and tests
revisit_trigger: Only a separately approved new downstream or field-level contract

decision: repository description, homepage, topics, and GitHub license recognition are post-release hygiene rather than 0.3 scientific scope
rationale: Repository discoverability should be repaired without coupling it to scientific engine design
revisit_trigger: Metadata is populated and license recognition verified

decision: the provisional 1.0.0 milestone is defined by stable contracts and evidence, not export count
rationale: Scientific stability depends on compatibility, validation, provenance, and performance baselines
revisit_trigger: 1.0 release-candidate acceptance review
